claims.statement: Agent spread selects exactly one lane per detected agent: `openwiki integrations install <codex|claude|opencode>` for v0.4.3 registry-supported hosts, otherwise the headless ladder where the agent directly drives `openwiki --init -p` / `openwiki --update -p`.

The registry lane `openwiki integrations install <host>` atomically copies the skill bundle to the host skill directory and edits the host MCP config while writing a `.openwiki-install.json` receipt; the MCP is delivered as `openwiki mcp --host <target>` and without this registration the OpenWiki skill (sequence tools openwiki_begin/next_page/submit_page/finish) is inert.

Receipt `.openwiki-install.json` records package, version (openwiki version), target, SHA-256 file hashes, and the exact mcpServerCommand (`openwiki` + `mcp --host <target>`); `openwiki integrations list` hash-verifies receipts and reports `installed`/`unchanged` vs `modified` (hash drift/hand-edits) vs `not-installed`.

Before touching any agent skill directory, spread enforces ownership partition via receipt: if `.openwiki-install.json` is present with matching target and intact hashes the host is treated as owned by the official lane, skipped entirely, and reported as such; `modified` requires explicit `--force` to overwrite (with backup path reported).

Kit code never hardcodes agent skill paths; all targets are derived at runtime from the registry via `openwiki integrations list` / `inspectInstallation`; bootstrap prefers `openwiki integrations install` where supported to avoid maintaining a path matrix that drifts (e.g., codex `~/.agents/skills/` vs `~/.codex/skills/`).

Installs source the bundle from the locally installed npm package at `<npm-root>/openwiki/integrations/openwiki` (not a tag-pinned GitHub tree); the receipt pins the openwiki version (`npm ls openwiki`) and updating is `npm i -g openwiki@latest` then re-run `openwiki integrations install <target>`, idempotent when version/hashes/command already match.

`openwiki integrations install` is transactional with staging, backup, and config-snapshot rollback; it rejects symlinked skill directories or any symlinked parent component and rejects non-directory parents, and cleans up the staging directory on failure so no half-install remains.

Per-host MCP config edits are registry-owned: codex `~/.codex/config.toml` (TOML installCodexMcpBlock with replaceableEntry detection), claude `~/.claude.json` or `.mcp.json` (JSON), opencode `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (JSONC); the installer snapshots configs and rolls back on commit failure.

Global ordering is enforced: `openwiki@latest` must be installed and resolvable on PATH before registering `openwiki mcp --host <target>` in host configs; verification is via `openwiki integrations list` returning `installed`/`unchanged` after install.

Bootstrap uses a two-lane execution model (EXECUTE when it can run locally vs INSTRUCT when sandboxed) with never-half-install semantics: a step that cannot execute prints the exact remaining copy-paste commands and exits clean without partial state, and idempotency is by detection of observable state (tools on PATH, `openspec/` present, markers, receipts) not a journal file.

After spread completes a per-agent report is produced naming each detected agent, the lane chosen (`openwiki integrations install <host>` vs headless), the outcome (`installed`/`unchanged`/`modified` via `openwiki integrations list`), and installer details including backup path on `--force`.

Shared integration patterns under `docs/integrations/patterns.md` codify that tool-native files are wiring (bootstrap files, rules, MCP config, local preferences) and `.agents/` files are the durable source of truth; product guides keep exact filenames/snippets while shared decisions live once in patterns.md.

Four pattern groups are defined (root AGENTS.md native/compatible; tool-specific bootstrap file; rules-based IDE wiring; persistent memory/runtime boundary) and the session export rule requires exporting durable evidence to `.agents/sessions/<folder>/` at task boundaries for cross-tool distillation instead of relying on private memory.
